structured_output.root_cause: In click 8.3.0, `Parameter.handle_parse_result` (test-repos/click/src/click/core.py:2536-2551) writes to the shared destination `ctx.params[self.name]` using a first-touch-wins guard (`self.name not in ctx.params`) and then commits `value if value is not UNSET else None`. For flag-value options sharing a destination (`--red`/`--green`/`--blue` all targeting `color`), only `--green` has `default=True`, which `Option.__init__` aligns to its `flag_value` ("green") at core.py:2771-2772; siblings keep `self.default = UNSET`, so their `consume_value` returns UNSET when no CLI/env/default_map input is given. With declaration order `--red, --green, --blue`, click processes `--red` first: the guard sees `color` is unclaimed, and line 2551 writes `None` (because its value is UNSET), claiming the slot. When `--green` is then processed, the guard `self.name not in ctx.params` is false, so its "green" default never reaches `ctx.params["color"]`, and `main` receives `None`. Reordering `--green` above `--red` lets `--green` win the first-touch race and write "green", which is why declaration order changes the result.

hypotheses.summary: Parameter.handle_parse_result's first-touch-wins guard combined with the UNSET→None write lets a non-contributing sibling claim the shared destination before the option with default=True can fill it.

supporting_evidence.note: Parameter.handle_parse_result: guard `self.name not in ctx.params` enforces first-touch wins; line 2551 writes `value if value is not UNSET else None`, converting a non-contribution into None inside the just-claimed slot
Parameter.consume_value returns UNSET when no CLI input, env, default_map, and self.default is UNSET

Option.__init__: `if self.default is True and self.flag_value is not UNSET: self.default = self.flag_value` — only --green (default=True) gets default aligned to flag_value; --red/--blue keep default=UNSET
`and self.name not in ctx.params` — first-touch wins semantics for shared-name parameters
`ctx.params[self.name] = value if value is not UNSET else None` writes None for a non-contributing option that won the first-touch race

Manual trace reproduces both reported outputs: order red,green,blue → ctx.params["color"] set to None by --red, locking out --green → None; order green,red,blue → --green claims first with "green" → "green"

rejected_hypotheses.reason: consume_value returns ("green", DEFAULT) for --green in isolation because core.py:2771-2772 sets self.default = self.flag_value when default is True; order-sensitivity only manifests when a sibling processed earlier has already written to ctx.params[name], so the regression is in the shared-name write guard in handle_parse_result, not per-option default resolution

unknowns: exact commit SHA in click 8.3.0 that introduced the guard/write at core.py:2536-2551
whether 8.2.x had a different write path that avoided the UNSET→None pre-emption
structured_output.next_best_action: In Parameter.handle_parse_result (test-repos/click/src/click/core.py:2536-2551), tighten the guard to also require `value is not UNSET` before writing ctx.params[self.name], then add a post-pass `ctx.params.setdefault(param.name, None)` for each declared exposed param to fill in still-missing names.
